videos.script:
In the JavaScript course you published a package. {{server}} Today the package is a server, and nobody installs it but you. That changes what package.json is for. It stops being a promise to strangers and becomes a description of how to run this one project.

{{start}} So you start the project the rest of this course builds, a link shortener, with a package.json written by hand. Then you install Express, ask for one package, and receive sixty-five. You will find out why each of them is there.

{{scripts}} Then the project's own commands, in scripts, and the difference between npm run and the newer node --run.

{{deploy}} Then the three things a server's dependencies need from you. Keeping them current. Installing exactly what was tested, with npm ci. And reading a security advisory, on an old Express with seven of them, and fixing it.

{{tests}} And last, the test runner Node brings with it. You will write three tests for the project's first module, and then break the module and watch one of them catch it.
